context: Parallel coordinates data visualization showing adversarial audit scores across 84 blocks, with brushable axes for filtering and hover-to-inspect tooltips
first_impression: A deliberately designed parallel coordinates chart with a scientifically-motivated Tol Sunset diverging palette and clean typographic hierarchy that reads as intentional rather than default.
what_works: The Tol Sunset color palette for disagreement encoding is a deliberate, non-default choice that creates clear visual signal — and the 'Disagreement (σ)' axis label is tinted in the high-disagreement red (#A50026), elegantly connecting the legend color to its axis. Typography hierarchy is confident: bold title, muted subtitle, weight-differentiated axis labels versus tick text.
what_doesnt: The 100px gradient legend bar labeled only 'low' and 'high' provides no numerical calibration, leaving the viewer unable to map colors to actual σ values without hovering. The fixed 940px chart width leaves a large dead zone on the right at wider viewport sizes — the container width is hardcoded rather than responsive, making the layout feel unfinished at the page level.
